patterns.key_values: dropdown panel ~378x406px @~1x, 2x3 card grid, near-white opaque ground, top segmented device switcher, trailing '...' more button, corner ~12-16pt; separate dense inline menu-bar readout strip with 3-letter vertical labels

2-column, ~16pt gutter, ~10-12pt card radius, near-borderless (~2-3% tonal separation), each card = title(secondary) + hero value(bold) + bespoke gauge/chart; grouping carried by content + padding, not by borders
segmented control as primary content/device navigation (iOS idiom on Mac); WidgetKit-style gauges: dashed/segmented donut ring, mirrored up/down histogram, diagonal-hatch empty battery slots

signature_moves: Fixed per-metric identity palette instead of the system accent: indigo #5953FD = storage, blue #2A9CF9 = processor, hot-pink #ED58AD <-> purple = network. Systematic across every card and shared verbatim with the iOS sibling, so each stat is pre-attentively distinguishable at a glance.

Custom WidgetKit-style gauge vocabulary with a consistent stroke language: segmented dashed donut (disk), symmetric up/down histogram (network), diagonal-hatched placeholder tiles (bluetooth) — bespoke data-viz, not stock AppKit controls.

Split personality by surface: a dense iStat-style native readout in the menu bar (3-letter vertical DSK/CPU/NET labels) opens into a colorful, roomy, consumer WidgetKit-style dropdown — austere-native glance layer, playful-consumer detail layer.
defects: Contrast Dilution (mild) — card containers separated by only ~2-3% tonal fill so container edges fall under 3:1; Bluetooth empty-slot diagonal-hatch tiles and tertiary metadata (Last 7 days, pill-tag labels) read too faint. Canon: give container edges >=3:1 or a stronger tonal step, and lift metadata to ~gray-500 rather than ~gray-300.

aesthetic.direction: Consumer telemetry dashboard, WidgetKit-flavored: near-white restrained ground with a committed multi-hue identity palette carrying the data-viz (full-palette on charts, restrained everywhere else) — light-mode, soft radii, chip pills; the iOS-widget aesthetic ported to a Mac menu-bar utility rather than an AppKit-pro readout.
peers: DataMan / iOS telemetry widgets (the colorful-consumer register)

psychology: Von Restorff / signal detection — one fixed hue per metric class makes each card's subject pre-attentively distinct before any label is read; strong for an at-a-glance monitor.
Aesthetic-usability effect — polished colorful gauges raise the perceived usability and trust of what is fundamentally a wall of numbers; polish is functional here, not cosmetic.
Miller/Cowan chunking — 6 cards in a 2x3 grid = 6 clean chunks (within the <=5-7 glance budget); each card self-contained.

Jakob's Law (softly violated) — iOS segmented-nav + WidgetKit cards depart from the Mac menu-bar-utility convention (iStat's dense native readout); trades native familiarity for cross-platform consistency with its own iOS app.
Serial-position / prime real estate — the most-load-bearing metric (Disk) sits top-left where the eye starts.
notes: Cover is a MARKETING COMPOSITE: Sequoia sunburst wallpaper (brand evidence), an iPhone frame running the iOS app (LINEAGE-CONTRAST ONLY, excluded from macOS canon), and the real macOS evidence = a menu-bar-extra dropdown panel + a menu-bar readout strip. The rounded dark menu-bar 'capsule' is a composite framing device, not a real system element. Lineage read as native (a genuine Mac menu-bar-extra utility, almost certainly multiplatform SwiftUI) but the design DIALECT is iOS/WidgetKit-derived — the iOS and macOS surfaces are visually near-identical, confirming a shared design system; therefore its density, segmented-as-nav, chip pills, and non-system accent are recorded as iOS TELLS, not learnable AppKit 'mac taste'. Catalyst cannot be fully ruled out from a still but menu-bar-extra + polish favors SwiftUI. Era read as big-sur (Sequoia-continuum vibrancy, opaque rounded panel) — NOT liquid-glass; no glass lensing observable, so material appearance is (insufficient-evidence). All pixel values (estimated) at an ASSUMED ~1x scale (panel 378px wide reads as ~1x for this content); no @2x chrome available to calibrate against. Only one macOS surface available; no dark mode, no settings/onboarding surfaces seen.
